summary: Per second on allocated vCPU, memory and disk, with free monthly allowances on every plan; Hobby is a $50 monthly minimum that is usable as usage.
sleeps: An idle timeout pauses a VM after a set period without network activity; the next start or request resumes it with memory intact.

egress.included: 50 GB on Free, 500 GB on Hobby and Pro
egress.note: Data transfer counts bytes crossing the datacenter boundary in either direction; traffic between your own VMs in a VPC is not billed.

plans.name: Free
plans.note: Free is a hard allowance: usage stops at the monthly limit instead of billing overage. Freestyle's pricing page says Free has no persistent VMs (its docs table says it does); the calculator follows the pricing page, so a machine whose disk is kept while stopped is priced on Hobby.

plans.name: Hobby
plans.note: Hobby is a $50 monthly minimum; the fee covers the first $50 of usage and only the excess is billed on top.

plans.name: Pro
plans.note: Pro is a $500 monthly minimum; the fee covers the first $500 of usage and only the excess is billed on top.

notes: The free allowances (200 vCPU-hours, 400 GiB-hours of memory, 60,000 GiB-hours of storage) apply on every plan, including Hobby and Pro.
Snapshot storage is not priced separately in the calculator. The pricing page lists only vCPU, memory, storage and data transfer, and the billable size of a snapshot is not published.
A paused VM bills storage but no compute. The product page's 'pay nothing while paused' claim conflicts with the pricing page; the rate card follows the pricing page.
Enterprise custom limits, measured-CPU billing, node-based pricing and a 99.99% SLA are not modelled because their prices are not published.

Free and persistence: the docs' plan table marks persistent VMs available on Free, but the pricing page's limit table marks them unavailable (both read 2026-10-30). The calculator follows the stricter pricing page, so a stopped-and-kept machine is priced on Hobby; if the docs are right, workload C would fit inside Free's allowances at $0.

upkeep.label: What you keep up
upkeep.detail: Freestyle updates its public base images, but your saved snapshots keep their installed versions, and VMs can run indefinitely, so updating what is installed is yours.

source.quote: Saved snapshots keep their installed versions when the public base image is updated
